Hundreds of millions of dollars have poured into the government account bankrolling President Donald Trump’s beautification projects in Washington, D.C. — and the administration is staying mum about where all that money’s coming from.

Financial records detailed in a Tuesday report from The New York Times showed that the National Park Service received close to $300 million in donations in September, nearly seven times the $50 million the agency had projected.

The funds went to an account originally set up to support all of the country’s national parks but has become a central funding source for Washington, D.C., renovations, like the new White House ballroom, botched revamp of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and plans to construct a triumphal arch.

The records did not include the source of the donations, and the Trump administration declined to share any information when approached by The Times.

Interior Department spokesperson Katie Martin did, however, celebrate the president’s attention to the capital, telling the paper, “President Donald J. Trump has done more to make our nation’s capital a shining beacon than any other president in the history of this country.”

The lack of transparency is raising serious questions among watchdog groups regarding donors and whether they are trying to curry favor with the White House through their money.

“Are the donors seeking certain government benefits?” Tony Irish, a former Interior Department lawyer who now works for the group Public Employees for Environmental Responsibility, asked The Times.

The National Park Service account has received a remarkable increase in donations since Trump returned to office last year, taking in approximately $790 million compared to the less than $100 million annual average from years prior.

Trump’s plans to put his personal mark on Washington have hit a number of snags in recent months. Judges have temporarily blocked work on the ballroom and intervened in the president’s designs for the arch. A legal battle is also currently playing out over Trump’s desire to redevelop one of the city’s public golf courses.
